en: a life with Luisa.
And the traditional life in this house
was never something I disliked, either.
All that's left is to await my father's decision,
and pray to God for a good reply.
She, too, strongly wished to marry you.
Even so, is a conclusion still far off?
I've decided.
note: No used_in; Stuart speaking, rows 1847-1849 read 'I've decided. I'll try telling my father / how I feel.'

en: I'll try telling my father
how I feel.
Thank you.
What should I do?
The more I think about it,
the further away a conclusion seems to get.
"Everything is decided apart from my will,"
that's what you said, if I recall.
note: Stern-register PLAYER quoting Stuart; the polite twin is #1913.

en: Yes, I did say that, but...
That may be so for work, but matchmaking
don't you refuse by your own choice?
That's right.
Among the maids who work for us,
note: No used_in; 'Among the maids ... there is a girl named "Luisa."'

en: there is a girl named "Luisa."
Actually, that girl and I are in love.
In this house, marriage is
the "job" of guarding our standing and bloodline.
Marrying Luisa is
even harder than becoming a writer.
In the end, whether it's work or marriage,
everything is decided apart from my will.
Do I choose the house, or my own will
note: Followed by M1#2 '...' (trailing off): 'Do I choose the house, or my own will...'

en: I hear matchmaking offers come up often.
You heard that from my mother, didn't you?
Besides not being able to become a writer,
the other pain I carry is, in fact, this.
Guarding this house means guarding its standing,
and protecting its bloodline.
Bloodline
note: Followed by three M1#180 (each '...') in msgs 74673 and 75260 = 9 dots. Add variants on M1#180 for msgs 74673 and 75260: en '.' so it reads 'Bloodline...'.

en: Is something the matter with the bloodline?
No, that's just my own affair.
Go on.
That is the root of my suffering.
If it were only about not becoming a writer,
I surely wouldn't suffer this much.
Why do you hesitate to take over the house?
Truth is, I wanted to become a writer.
I still do.
My father's opposition was no half measure.
With no siblings, the one road chosen for me
is to protect the Stanberg family.
But something hurts even more than that.
There is no road but protecting this house.
Born into the Stanberg family, is that
my fate?
Welcome to the Stanberg house.
note: Shared by Stuart, Lord Stanberg and Luisa; works for all three.

en: I am Stuart.
The Stanberg house?
If you're not from around here,
it's understandable that you wouldn't know.
Our ancestors, as lords, governed this region
for a great many years.
These days the mayor is the center of politics,
but our family's power is still immense.
You talk of your own house like an outsider,
note: Complete clause so it works with the polite continuation #1924/#1925 (slice 024); #1903/#1904 carry the sentence end.

en: but is it your own family's power that
note: Continues into #1904 'displeases you?'. Polite twin #1924/#1925 should end with a question about disliking the family's power.

en: displeases you?
Even without working, my life as a noble is
guaranteed. It's true that I'm in such a
fortunate position.
But that also means losing all freedom to do
anything but protect this house.
She also wished very strongly
note: Cut after 'wished very strongly' so #1911 holds 'to marry you.'

en: to marry you.
Even so, is a conclusion still far off?
I believe that is what you said.
That may be so for work, but
with matchmaking, isn't it your own choice
to refuse them?
I hear matchmaking offers come up often.
To protect this house is to guard its standing,
No, that's just my own affair.
